results.title: Bloomery iron smelting in the Daye County (Hubei): Technological traditions in Qing China - ScienceDirect
results.content: # Bloomery iron smelting in the Daye County (Hubei): Technological traditions in Qing China. China is widely accepted as the birthplace and shrine of the blast furnace, with bloomery iron technology largely believed to be scant before the Han Dynasty, and virtually inexistent afterwards. Challenging this traditional picture, this paper presents the material characterisation and reverse engineering of the primary smelting of bloomery iron at five metal production sites, located in close proximity of each other in the Daye County in Hubei Province, China, and in operation during the middle Qing Dynasty. The earliest cast iron fragment found so far in China is dated to the 8th century BC (Zou, 2000) whereas large quantities of excavated material show that cast iron production became the prevailing technique for iron metallurgy in the Central Plains of China no later than the 6th century BC (Han and Ko, 2007; Wagner, 2008; Chen, 2014; Liu et al., 2014).

results.title: Extraction and separation of copper and iron from copper smelting slag: A review - ScienceDirect
results.content: # Extraction and separation of copper and iron from copper smelting slag: A review. A large amount of copper smelting slag (CSS) containing valuable elements such as copper and iron is produced through smelting. CSS is a kind of solid waste slag produced in the process of pyrometallurgical copper smelting (Piatak et al., 2015; Sarfo et al., 2017). The typical copper smelting process flow of chalcopyrite is shown in Fig. 1 (Tian et al., 2021). Consequently, it is imperative to realize the efficient development and utilization of CSS resources, improve the self-sufficiency rate of copper concentrate and iron concentrate, and strengthen environmental protection by strengthening independent technological innovation (Sarfo et al., 2017; Starodub et al., 2016; Wang, Zhu et al., 2022). This work mainly reviews and combs the physical separation methods, chemical separation methods and combined separation methods used to separate and extract copper and iron from CSS, and puts forward a new route to treat CSS by microwave fluidization roasting. In the smelting process, the composition of smelting slag will change greatly under different influencing factors (copper ore raw materials, flux, smelting mode, etc.). According to different copper smelting properties, various beneficiation and metallurgical methods were generally used to extract and recover valuable metals, including flotation, roasting followed by magnetic separation, leaching, smelting and other processes. ### Base metals recovery from copper smelter slag by oxidising leaching and solvent extraction. ### Green and efficient utilization of waste ferric-oxide desulfurizer to clean waste copper slag by the smelting reduction-sulfurizing process. ### Technological scheme for copper slag processing. ### Recovery of iron and removal of hazardous elements from waste copper slag via a novel aluminothermic smelting reduction (ASR) process. ### The pH-dependent leaching behavior of slags from various stages of a copper smelting process: environmental implications. ### A novel process to upgrade the copper slag by direct reduction-magnetic separation with the addition of Na2CO3 and CaO. ### Research status of iron recovery from copper slag and proposal of new methods. ### Recovery of value metals from copper smelter slag by ammonium chloride treatment. ### Characteristics and mechanism of reduction and smelting-separation process of copper slag. ### Cleaner recycling of iron from waste copper slag by using walnut shell char as green reductant.

results.title: Iron Smelting in Cherrapunjee for 2000 years say Scientists.
results.content: Radiocarbon dating of charcoal from iron slag revealed evidence of continuous iron smelting in the Khasi Hills, Meghalaya, NE India spanning the last two millennia. The slag layer, which is dated to 2040 ± 80 years BP (353 BC–AD 128), is the earliest iron smelting site studied in the entire region of NE India. The presence of wüstite, fayalite, glass and metal iron, together with spinels such as hercynite in the slag, indicates that it was an acid product of a bloomery iron-making process. These are clearly visible in the case of the central part of Meghalaya, which is inhabited by the Khasi, an Austro-Asiatic speaking people, representing the remnants of an ancient migration from Southeast Asia (11,12). The aim of this communication is to estimate the temporal extent of iron smelting in the Khasi Hills and to present an analysis of the technological process of iron production development during that time.

results.title: Extraction and separation of copper and iron from copper smelting slag: A review - ScienceDirect
results.content: # Extraction and separation of copper and iron from copper smelting slag: A review. A large amount of copper smelting slag (CSS) containing valuable elements such as copper and iron is produced through smelting. With the increasing shortage of copper resources, the full recovery of valuable elements in CSS plays an important part in resource utilization improvement, strengthen environmental protection and promote China's circular economy. In this study, a variety of methods for extracting and separating copper and iron from CSS are reported. This review provides guidance for the selection and development of secondary resources of CSS or other solid wastes containing iron and copper. CSS is a kind of solid waste slag produced in the process of pyrometallurgical copper smelting (Piatak et al., 2015; Sarfo et al., 2017). According to different copper smelting properties, a variety of beneficiation and metallurgical methods are generally used for extraction and recovery of copper.
